| [r1 — Every fold gains from more training mice; mice differ far more than folds](r1-cv-predictability.md) | draft: awaiting the claims check and the first author's review | How well does the GRU predict a mouse it never saw, and does that hold for every mouse, not only the 149 test mice that every earlier held-out number spent? Studies 01 and 02 measured held-out prediction once, on one split; a model ranking, a scaling curve or a per-mouse residual built on that split could reflect which mice happened to be in it. | **F1.** Held-out likelihood (trial-pooled, left/right on engaged trials) rises from D = 10 to full size in all 5 folds, by +0.0123 ± 0.0007 within each fold's own mice (mean ± SEM, n = 5 folds).<br>**F2.** Predictability is a property of the mouse: per-mouse held-out likelihood spans 0.623 to 0.825 (5th to 95th percentile, n = 763 mice), and the two disjoint halves of each mouse's sessions agree (Pearson r = 0.96).<br>**F3.** The 3-way GRU predicts left/right better than the 2-way GRU in all 5 folds (+0.0016 ± 0.0001, SEM over folds), and the gain sits on the first engaged trial after an ignore: +0.034 there, where 4.5% of trials carry 118% of the gain.<br>**F4.** The fold-to-fold spread (SD 0.0029) is within which-mice sampling (random 5-way splits of the same mice: median SD 0.0061, P(random ≥ real) = 0.95); the original test fold scores 0.0024 below all 763 mice. |
